small_guidance:
- The conv_transpose now dominates runtime (fast_p ~1.19 with the fused pool/htanh/mean kernel already saturating); minor tuning of BLOCK/num_warps in the fused tail kernel will not move the needle. Within the existing fused kernel, try BLOCK=1024 with num_warps=4 — H_out*W_out=16384 per program, so 16 iters of 1024 may have better occupancy than 4 iters of 4096.
- Consider precomputing `inv_count` as a constexpr by passing H_out and W_out as constexpr (they are static at 128x128), letting Triton fold the division.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose2d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: with stride=1, padding=1, kernel=3, the transposed conv is equivalent to a plain conv2d with the weight flipped on spatial dims and channels swapped (in_channels↔out_channels). Rewrite as a direct conv2d Triton kernel (im2col-style GEMM, one program per (N, OC tile, output spatial tile)) — this is the heaviest op and the biggest headroom.
- Fuse the entire pipeline into the conv epilogue: after the GEMM accumulator produces conv output for a 2x2 spatial tile, reduce via max (the maxpool window), clamp to [-1,1], and atomically/locally accumulate into a per-(N,C) partial sum. A second tiny kernel finishes the mean+tanh. This removes the full intermediate (128,64,256,256) tensor materialization, which is currently ~2GB of memory traffic.
- Alternatively, use channels-last layout for the conv output so the 2x2 maxpool reads are contiguous along C, enabling vectorized loads in the reduction stage.
